- while the icons app works mostly nice, it now has started to refuse me more icons-adds. This applet is the one that should be feeding a NEW icon dropdown in face-apps, it doesn't. Apps, still uses the legacy icon dropdown, with the hard-coded table from kernel.js.

chat.text: explain.
Taking: reading the Icons app, the Apps icon field and what the face loads, then I explain.

What is behind each:

- Icons refusing adds: every add loads the whole set and saves it back whole, 271 icons, 10.9 KB. The app refuses for only three reasons: a duplicate, too many keywords, or a save that failed (it then says not saved: and why). The node puts no size limit on the file, but on the face both trips go as one sealed message each, so a growing set can outgrow the face link.
- The old dropdown: the Apps app's icon field is the new list, read from the Icons app's set. The old one, with kernel.js's built-in table, is still drawn by the Groups app (group-manager) and by the old home shell's elements.
- kernel.js on the face: the face loads the home node's index.html scripts in order, kernel.js among them, because the shell elements and apps still read the kernel's members (its constants, util, the jobs stream). It goes when those move onto the spirit object; G32 moved the node calls, not those.

What does the line beside Add say when it refuses, and which screen showed you the old dropdown?

i searched i icons for '🤹'  it's no there, then try to add it, with one keyword only, icons says: "not saved: refused". it has been doing this for a while, with every icon i tried to add.

i verified that the icon-dropdown shows icons that i added in icons, and don't exist in kernel.js. aaccepted. in fact all your remarks are accepted, except the one i mentioned above.

The icons refusal, what I found:

- at home the same save works: the whole set with your icon added saves (204), so the node takes it
- on the face it travels sealed through the relay to your node and back, and somewhere on that way it is refused; the refusal there carries its reason as text but no code, and the spirit object keeps only the code, so the screen says refused and the reason is lost
- likeliest cause: every add sends the whole set (now 10.9 KB, about 18 KB sealed), close to what one face request may carry; not proven

Proposal, in two steps: first the refusal shows its reason on screen (a small fix in the spirit object), you try once more and we read the real cause; then the fix for that cause. Add an item for the first step?
add item to fix this

items.title: Icons on the face: a refusal says why, and adding works
items.creator: claude-windows
items.box:
ICONS ON THE FACE: A REFUSAL SAYS WHY, AND ADDING WORKS

- On the face, adding an icon in the Icons app says not saved: refused, for every icon; at home the same save is taken.
- A refusal on its way to the face keeps its reason: where the node, the face door or the relay answers with words and no code, the spirit object carries the words, and the Icons app shows them beside Add.
- Then the cause the words name is fixed, so an icon added on the face is saved and shows in every icon list.
- The Icons app keeps writing the one set it owns, shell/icons/iconSet.json; a set too large to travel is not the answer to cut.

Where: face/spirit.js, shell/icons/icons.js, and the hop the reason names.

There it is: the relay takes at most 23552 bytes for one face request, and your save came to 23608, 56 over.

The fix, as agreed, without touching the relay:

- the face splits a sealed request too large for one trip into pieces, each its own call under the limit; the relay passes them on as it does any call and still reads none of it
- your node collects the pieces by their id (bounded in count, size and time), opens the whole once the last is in, and answers it on the last piece

i lost my face-login on spirit-3 it wants me to re-log-in, and the emails are not reaching my inbox....

What the relay does there, read from its code:

- a face login is kept on your member row and survives a restart, but it expires after a stretch of no use; then it asks again
- the login mail goes out at most once a minute and five times an hour; past that it sends nothing and says nothing
- a mail that fails to send is dropped without a word in the log, so a broken mail driver looks exactly like this

I cannot see spirit-3. How many times did you ask for the mail in the last hour, and what does journalctl -u spirit-relay -n 50 say?
i've been using the face constantly to verify fixes, and we said my login lasts for 7 days of idleness, so there's a bug there somewhere

Found it, I think: the relay hands your browser the login cookie with a 7-day life only when you log in, and never renews it.

- each use moves the relay's own deadline 7 days on, but your browser throws the cookie away 7 days after the login itself, however busy you were
- if your last login was about a week ago, that is what happened
- the fix: the relay renews the cookie whenever the face shows it is still logged in (its state check); a relay change, so a tag

The missing mails are a separate question: past one a minute or five an hour the relay sends none and says nothing.

Add an item for the cookie renewal?
mailgun logs show nothing

Then the relay never handed mailgun a mail. In its code that happens, silently, in three cases:

- the cap: more than one ask a minute or five an hour; it clears within the hour
- no mail driver loaded: relay-state/mail.json missing or unreadable since the restart
- what you typed into the login field is not exactly the email on your member row (any case, but no spaces)

On spirit-3: does ls ~/SpiritOS/spirit/run/relay-state/mail.json show the file, and does journalctl -u spirit-relay -n 50 mention mail?
the login doesn't even exist for 7 days yet
and mailgun shows no transactions for the last 24 hours (that's how far back their logs go.)

Then the cookie is not it, and I read the relay again: your login is kept on your member row and found again after a restart, and its hash does not change, so it should still be good.

My best guess now: while spirit-3 restarted, the face asked whether you are logged in, got no answer, showed the login screen, and never asked again.

Would you reload the face page (F5) and tell me whether it comes up logged in?

Nothing in 24 hours means the relay has not tried to send at all, not the hourly cap: either no mail driver is loaded (relay-state/mail.json gone or unreadable) or it never gets that far. The file and journalctl on spirit-3 tell which.
